## animate.ts

The JS spring engine for DOM elements.

`animate()` springs an element's *motion channels* — CSS custom properties
that the `.motion` / `.tilt` classes turn into real transforms:

| channel | custom property | unit (number written unitless) | rest |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `x` / `y` | `--mx` / `--my` | px | 0 |
| `scale` | `--ms` | factor | 1 |
| `rotate` | `--mr` | deg | 0 |
| `opacity` | `--mo` | 0..1 | 1 |
| `rotateX` / `rotateY` | `--rx` / `--ry` | deg | 0 |
| `--anything` | written as-is | — | 0 |

JavaScript only ever writes custom properties; the stylesheet owns the
real `translate` / `scale` / `rotate` / `opacity` / `transform`.

### `type MotionChannel`

A named motion channel, mapped to a custom property read by `.motion` / `.tilt`.

### `type MotionValues`

Target values by channel name; any `--custom` property may be sprung too.

### `interface AnimateOptions`

Options for {@link animate}.

- `spring` :: The spring to use (preset name or partial config). Defaults to `'snappy'`.
- `velocity` :: Initial velocities (units per second) by channel name, overriding the carried-over velocity.
- `instant` :: Jump straight to the targets with no animation.
- `onUpdate` :: Called after every frame with the current value of each animated channel (keyed as passed in).

### `interface AnimationHandle`

A running animation.

- `finished` :: Resolves when every channel has settled, been stopped, or been taken over by a newer `animate()` call.
- `stop` :: Stop this animation's channels where they are (velocity is discarded).

### `function toProp`

Map a channel name (`x`, `--mx`, `--custom`) to its custom property, or `null` if unknown.

### `function animate`

Spring an element's motion channels to target values. Interruptible: each element's per-channel position and velocity live in a `WeakMap`, so a new call continues from the current value *and* velocity — gestures never jump. All running springs share one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (fixed-step RK4 integration, clamped frame time) that stops when idle. With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `globalMotion.scale === 0`, or `instant: true`, values jump to their targets. The element should carry the `.motion` class (and `.tilt` for `rotateX`/`rotateY`) so the custom properties become real transforms. @example ```ts animate(card, { y: -8, scale: 1.02 }, { spring: 'bouncy' }); ``` @param node The element to animate. @param to Target values by channel (`x`, `y`, `scale`, `rotate`, `opacity`, `rotateX`, `rotateY`, `--custom`). @param options Spring, initial velocities, `instant`, `onUpdate`.

### `function getMotion`

Read the current sprung value of a channel on a node. Returns the channel's rest value (`1` for `scale`/`opacity`, else `0`) if it has never been set. @param node The element. @param channel A channel name (`x`, `scale`, …), its property (`--mx`), or a `--custom` property.

### `function getVelocity`

Read the current velocity (units per second) of a channel on a node; `0` when at rest. @param node The element. @param channel A channel name, its property, or a `--custom` property.

### `function setMotion`

Set channels immediately, with no animation. Resets their velocity and interrupts any spring running on them. @param node The element. @param values Values by channel (`x`, `y`, `scale`, …, `--custom`).

## attachments.ts

Motion attachments — `{@attach …}` factories for gestures, scroll and layout.

Every attachment writes ONLY CSS custom properties (plus, for `inView`, a
state class); the stylesheet's `.motion` / `.tilt` classes turn them into
real transforms. Every attachment cleans up on teardown and honours reduced
motion (`prefers-reduced-motion` or `globalMotion.scale === 0`).

### `interface FrameJob`

A job in the shared scroll frame: every `read` runs before any `write`.

### `function addScrollJob`

Register a scroll-linked job; shares one passive scroll/resize listener and one rAF across all jobs.

### `function observe`

IntersectionObserver wrapper shared by `inView` and `reveal`. Returns a disconnect function.

### `function throttled`

rAF-coalesce a pointer handler: only the latest event per frame is processed.

### `function vars`

Bind CSS custom properties to an element — the sanctioned way to pass dynamic values to the stylesheet. Keys may be given with or without the leading `--`; `null`/`undefined` removes the property. Numbers are written unitless. Called inline in a template it re-runs whenever its arguments change. @example ```svelte <div class="fill" {@attach vars({ value: progress })}></div> ``` @param values Custom property values by name.

### `function magnetic`

Pull the element toward the pointer while it is within `radius` px of the element's bounds; it springs back when the pointer moves away. Mouse and pen only. Requires the `.motion` class. Disabled under reduced motion. @param options `strength` (0..1, default `0.35`), `radius` (px beyond the bounds, default `40`), `spring` (default `'snappy'`).

### `function tilt`

3D tilt toward the pointer. Writes `--rx`/`--ry` (and `--ms` for the lift scale). Requires the `.tilt` class (plus `.motion` for the scale). With `glare`, also writes the pointer position as `--px`/`--py` percentages for a highlight layer. Disabled under reduced motion. @param options `max` tilt in degrees (default `10`), `scale` while hovered (default `1.02`), `spring` (default `'snappy'`), `glare` (default `false`).

### `function press`

Spring the element's scale down while pressed — pointer, or Enter/Space from the keyboard — and back on release. Requires the `.motion` class. Disabled under reduced motion. @param options `scale` while pressed (default `0.96`), `spring` (default `'stiff'`).

### `function hover`

Spring lift while hovered (mouse/pen) or keyboard-focused (`:focus-visible` on the element or a descendant). Requires the `.motion` class. Disabled under reduced motion. @param options `scale` (default `1.02`), `y` offset in px (default `-4`, i.e. up), `spring` (default `'snappy'`).

### `function pointer`

Track the pointer over the element as `--px`/`--py` (for spotlights and gradients), rAF-throttled. With `unit: 'fraction'` (default) the values are `0..1` across the element's box — use `calc(var(--px) * 100%)`; with `unit: 'px'` they are unitless pixel offsets from the top-left corner — use `calc(var(--px) * 1px)`. Not motion, so it runs under reduced motion too. @param options `unit`: `'fraction'` (default) or `'px'`.

### `function inView`

Toggle a class (default `in`) when the element scrolls into view, via IntersectionObserver — pair it with CSS enter states. Where IntersectionObserver is unavailable the class is added immediately. @param options `once` (default `true`: stop observing after the first entry), `amount` visible fraction (default `0.2`), `margin` (root margin), `class` (default `'in'`), `onEnter`, `onLeave`.

### `function reveal`

Spring the element in from an offset state when it scrolls into view. The element starts at `{ x, y, scale, opacity }` and springs to rest. With `once: false` it springs back out when it leaves. Requires the `.motion` class. Under reduced motion the element is simply shown at rest. @param options `x` (px, default `0`), `y` (px, default `24`), `scale` (default `1`), `opacity` (default `0`), `delay` (ms, default `0`), `spring` (default `'gentle'`), `once` (default `true`), `amount` (default `0.2`).

### `function stagger`

Number a container's items for staggered CSS motion: writes `--i` (the item's stagger index) on each item and `--stagger` (the step, e.g. `60ms`) on the container, so CSS can use `transition-delay: calc(var(--i) * var(--stagger))`. Re-indexes when the child list changes. Under reduced motion `--stagger` is `0ms`. @param options `selector` for items (default: direct children), `step` in ms (default `60`), `from`: `'first'` (default), `'last'` or `'center'`.

### `interface DragState`

The drag gesture's state, passed to the drag callbacks.

- `x` :: Current offset on x (px, the `--mx` channel).
- `y` :: Current offset on y (px, the `--my` channel).
- `dx` :: Pointer movement on x since the drag started (px).
- `dy` :: Pointer movement on y since the drag started (px).
- `vx` :: Pointer velocity on x (px/s).
- `vy` :: Pointer velocity on y (px/s).

### `function drag`

Make the element draggable with springs. Uses pointer capture; the element should carry `.motion` (for the offset), `touch-none` (so touch drags are not scrolls) and usually `select-none`. Bounds are offsets relative to the resting position: `'parent'` keeps it inside its parent's box, a function returns a container `DOMRect`, or pass explicit `{ left, right, top, bottom }` offset limits. Past a bound the element rubber-bands by `elastic`. On release with `momentum`, the release velocity carries it on and it springs to rest inside the bounds; with `snapBack` it springs home. A drag that moved suppresses the following click. Under reduced motion dragging still works but release settles instantly. @param options `axis` (`'both'`), `bounds`, `snapBack` (`false`), `momentum` (`true`), `elastic` (0..1, `0.35`), `spring` (`'snappy'`), `disabled`, `onDragStart`, `onDrag`, `onDragEnd`.

### `function parallax`

Scroll-linked parallax: offsets the element by `speed` × its distance from the viewport centre, written to `--my` (or `--mx`). Positive speeds lag behind the scroll (background feel), negative ones lead it. Shares one passive scroll listener and one rAF (all reads before all writes) with every other scroll attachment. Requires the `.motion` class. Off under reduced motion. @param options `speed` (-1..1, default `0.2`), `axis` (`'y'` default, or `'x'`).

### `function scrollProgress`

Write scroll progress `0..1` to `--value` on the element (progress bars, scroll-linked fills). `target: 'page'` (default) tracks the document's scroll; `'element'` tracks the element's own passage through the viewport (0 as it enters, 1 as it leaves). Shares the scroll frame with `parallax`. @param options `target` (`'page'` | `'element'`), `axis` (`'y'` default, or `'x'`).

### `function createFlip`

FLIP layout animation with springs. Attach `flip.attach` to a container; call `read()` before the DOM changes and `play()` after it (`await tick()` first), or just `await flip.run(() => …)`. Items are matched across the change by `data-flip-id`; each springs from its old position (and size, as a uniform scale when the aspect ratio is kept) to its new one — interruptible, carrying velocity. New items fade/scale in. Items need the `.motion` class. Under reduced motion layout changes are instant. @example ```svelte <script lang="ts"> const flip = createFlip({ spring: 'snappy' }); let items = $state(['a', 'b', 'c']); const shuffle = () => flip.run(() => { items = items.toReversed(); }); </script> <ul {@attach flip.attach}> {#each items as id (id)}<li class="motion" data-flip-id={id}>{id}</li>{/each} </ul> ``` @param options `spring` (default `'snappy'`), `selector` for items (default `[data-flip-id]`).

## global.svelte.ts

Global motion state shared by every part of the motion layer.
Internal module — the public surface re-exports from `animate.ts` and
`spring.svelte.ts`.

### `const globalMotion`

The global motion switch for the JS spring engine. - `1` — normal speed (default). - `0` — JS motion disabled: every animation jumps straight to its target, exactly as with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. - Other positive values scale durations: `2` runs springs at half speed, `0.5` at double speed (mirrors a CSS duration multiplier). Reactive (`$state`), so the theme runtime can set it and `reducedMotion` reflects the change. Never reassign the object — set `globalMotion.scale`.

### `const reducedMotion`

Reactive reduced-motion flag: `true` when the user prefers reduced motion OR `globalMotion.scale === 0`. SSR-safe — the media query is created lazily on first read in the browser, and reads `false` on the server.

## loop.ts

The single shared animation-frame loop and the spring integrator.
Internal module: `animate()` and `SpringValue` both register tickers here,
so however many springs run there is exactly one `requestAnimationFrame`
chain, and it stops as soon as nothing is moving.

### `type Ticker`

A per-frame callback. Receives the clamped, time-scaled step in seconds; returns `false` when idle.

### `const MAX_DT`

Largest real frame gap simulated in one frame (a backgrounded tab must not explode the simulation).

### `const STEP`

Fixed integration sub-step (seconds).

### `const MAX_STEPS`

Upper bound on sub-steps per frame.

### `function addTicker`

Register a ticker; starts the loop if it was idle. Browser-only.

### `function removeTicker`

Remove a ticker. The loop stops on its own once the set is empty.

### `interface SpringState`

Mutable spring state: position and velocity.

### `function integrate`

Advance `state` toward `target` by `dt` seconds with fixed-step RK4 (sub-steps of at most 1/240 s). Mutates and returns `state`.

## spring.svelte.ts

Rune-based spring values for component state.

### `class SpringValue`

A reactive, spring-driven number. Setting `target` animates `current` along the spring; reading `current` in a template or `$derived` re-renders every frame while it moves. Retargeting mid-flight keeps the velocity, so motion stays continuous. Shares the motion layer's single rAF loop and honours reduced motion (jumps to the target). SSR-safe. @example ```svelte <script lang="ts"> import { SpringValue, vars } from '@fractaldesign/fractalsvelte-ui/motion'; const width = new SpringValue(0, 'gentle'); </script> <div class="fill" {@attach vars({ value: width.current })}></div> <button onclick={() => (width.target = 0.8)}>Grow</button> ```

- `spring` :: The spring used for subsequent motion (preset name or partial config).
- `current` :: The current animated value (reactive, read-only — set `target` or call `set()`).
- `target` :: The value being animated toward (reactive). Assigning it starts the spring.
- `velocity` :: The current velocity in units per second. Assign to impart momentum.
- `set` :: Animate to `value`. Resolves when the spring settles (or is stopped or jumped). @param value The new target. @param opts `instant` jumps with no animation; `velocity` sets the starting velocity (units/s).
- `stop` :: Stop where it is: `target` becomes `current` and velocity is discarded.

## spring.ts

### `interface SpringConfig`

The spring solver — pure maths, no DOM, no imports. This module is imported both by the library (the JS spring engine, the Svelte transitions) and by `scripts/gen-springs.ts` under plain Node, which is why it imports nothing and uses only erasable TypeScript syntax. Model: a damped harmonic oscillator `m·x'' = −k·(x − to) − c·x'`, solved analytically for the under-, critically- and over-damped cases.

- `stiffness` :: Spring constant `k` — higher is faster and tighter.
- `damping` :: Damping coefficient `c` — higher removes more oscillation. Critical damping is `2·√(k·m)`.
- `mass` :: Mass `m` — higher is heavier and slower.

### `type SpringPreset`

The named spring presets shared by CSS (`--spring-<name>`) and JS.

### `type SpringInput`

A preset name, or a partial config merged over the `snappy` preset.

### `const springs`

The preset table, in physical units with mass 1. | preset | feel | settle | overshoot | |:--|:--|:--|:--| | `stiff` | very fast, no overshoot | ≈ 225 ms | none | | `snappy` | quick, near-critically damped | ≈ 355 ms | < 1 % | | `gentle` | soft | ≈ 560 ms | < 1 % | | `bouncy` | playful, visible overshoot | ≈ 690 ms | ≈ 15 % | | `slow` | deliberate, large surfaces | ≈ 900 ms | none |

### `const REST_DELTA`

Default rest threshold, as a fraction of the travelled distance.

### `function resolveSpring`

Resolve a preset name or partial config into a complete {@link SpringConfig}. Partial configs are merged over the `snappy` preset; non-positive or non-finite values fall back to the preset's. @param input A preset name or partial config. Defaults to `'snappy'`.

### `function solve`

Displacement and velocity of the oscillator (relative to `to`) at time `t`.

### `function springPosition`

Analytic damped-harmonic-oscillator position at time `t` (seconds), handling the under-, critically- and over-damped cases exactly. @param config The physical spring. @param t Time in seconds since release. @param from Start position. Defaults to `0`. @param to Target (rest) position. Defaults to `1`. @param velocity Initial velocity in units per second. Defaults to `0`.

### `function springVelocity`

Analytic velocity (units per second) of the oscillator at time `t` (seconds). @param config The physical spring. @param t Time in seconds since release. @param from Start position. Defaults to `0`. @param to Target (rest) position. Defaults to `1`. @param velocity Initial velocity in units per second. Defaults to `0`.

### `function springDuration`

Settle time in milliseconds for a unit move (0 → 1, at rest): the first moment after which the position stays within `restDelta` of the target and the velocity stays below `restDelta × 10` per second. Results are cached. @param input A preset name or partial config. Defaults to `'snappy'`. @param restDelta Rest threshold as a fraction of the distance. Defaults to `0.002`.

### `function segmentDistance`

Perpendicular distance from point p to the segment a–b (in normalised plot space).

### `function simplify`

Ramer–Douglas–Peucker simplification: keep only points that matter.

### `function fmt`

Format a number with fixed precision and no trailing zeros (`-0` → `0`).

### `function springEasing`

A CSS `linear()` easing sampled from the spring, plus its settle duration — true spring curves in plain CSS transitions and animations. Output is deterministic: values to 3 decimals, stops to 2, redundant points dropped. @param input A preset name or partial config. Defaults to `'snappy'`. @param samples Number of samples over the duration before simplification. Defaults to `40`. @returns `{ easing: 'linear(…)', duration: <ms> }`.

### `function springEase`

An easing function `(t: 0..1) => value` that follows the spring (it may overshoot 1). Pair it with {@link springDuration} of the same input — e.g. for Svelte transitions. `ease(0) === 0` and `ease(1) === 1` exactly. @param input A preset name or partial config. Defaults to `'snappy'`.

## transitions.ts

Svelte transition functions driven by real spring curves.

Each returns `{ delay, duration, easing, css }` where `duration` is the
spring's settle time (`springDuration`) and `easing` follows the spring
itself (`springEase`) — so `bouncy` really overshoots. Svelte runs the `css`
keyframes via the Web Animations API. Under reduced motion every transition
becomes a short plain opacity fade.

### `interface SpringTransitionParams`

Parameters shared by every spring transition.

- `spring` :: The spring (preset name or partial config). Defaults to `'snappy'`.
- `delay` :: Delay before the transition starts, in ms. Defaults to `0`.

### `function springFade`

Fade in/out along a spring curve. @param node The transitioning element. @param params `spring`, `delay`.

### `function springFly`

Fly in/out from an offset, springing into place (overshoot included). @param node The transitioning element. @param params `spring`, `delay`, `x`/`y` offset in px (default `y: 16`), `opacity` at the offset (default `0`).

### `function springScale`

Scale in/out from `start`, with spring overshoot. @param node The transitioning element. @param params `spring`, `delay`, `start` scale (default `0.9`), `opacity` at the start (default `0`).

### `function springBlur`

Blur and fade in/out, with an optional vertical drift. @param node The transitioning element. @param params `spring`, `delay`, `amount` of blur in px (default `8`), `y` drift in px (default `0`).

### `function springSlide`

Collapse/expand the element's height (or width with `axis: 'x'`), including padding, margin and border, along a spring curve. Overshoot is clamped so surrounding layout never bounces. @param node The transitioning element. @param params `spring`, `delay`, `axis` (`'y'` default, or `'x'`).

## view-transitions.ts

View Transitions: typed page/state transitions with a graceful fallback.

The stylesheet styles `::view-transition-*` per type class on `<html>`
(`.vt-fade`, `.vt-slide`, …). This module only tags `<html>` with the class
for the transition's lifetime and writes origin custom properties.

### `type ViewTransitionType`

The built-in transition styles; each maps to the class `vt-<type>` on `<html>`.

### `interface NavigationLike`

The minimal shape of a SvelteKit navigation that the view-transition wiring needs.

- `from` :: Where the navigation came from.
- `to` :: Where the navigation is going.
- `type` :: The navigation type (`link`, `goto`, `popstate`, `form`, …).
- `delta` :: For history navigations, the number of steps (negative = back).
- `complete` :: Resolves once the navigation has completed.

### `type OnNavigateLike`

A SvelteKit-compatible `onNavigate` registration function.

### `interface ViewTransitionSetupOptions`

Options for {@link setupViewTransitions}.

- `type` :: The transition type, or a function choosing it per navigation (e.g. back → `'slide-back'`). Defaults to `'fade'`.

### `const supportsViewTransitions`

Whether `document.startViewTransition` is available (always `false` during SSR).

### `function startViewTransition`

Run `update` inside `document.startViewTransition`, tagging `<html>` with the class `vt-<type>` for the transition's duration. For `'reveal'` (a circular wipe) the origin is written to `--vt-x`/`--vt-y` on `<html>` as px lengths, and `--vt-r` holds the radius (px) needed to cover the viewport from it. Falls back to calling `update` directly when the API is unsupported, under reduced motion, or for type `'none'`. Resolves when the transition finishes (or right after `update` in the fallback); rejects if `update` throws. @param update The DOM/state change to animate. @param options `type` (default `'fade'`), `origin` (a point, a pointer event, or an element's centre).

### `function setupViewTransitions`

Wire SvelteKit navigations into view transitions. Kit-agnostic: pass your app's own `onNavigate` from `$app/navigation` (call this in the root layout during component init). Hash-only navigations are skipped. @example ```svelte <script lang="ts"> import { onNavigate } from '$app/navigation'; import { setupViewTransitions } from '@fractaldesign/fractalsvelte-ui/motion'; setupViewTransitions(onNavigate, { type: (nav) => ((nav.delta ?? 0) < 0 ? 'slide-back' : 'slide') }); </script> ``` @param onNavigate SvelteKit's `onNavigate` (or any compatible registration function). @param options `type`: a fixed type or a function of the navigation. Defaults to `'fade'`.

### `function vtName`

Give an element a shared-element identity for view transitions: writes `--vt-name` (the `.vt-name` class turns it into `view-transition-name`). Names are sanitised to a valid CSS identifier; `null`/`undefined` clears it. Each name must be unique on the page at transition time. @param name The shared-element name, e.g. `card-${id}`.

## index.ts

`@fractaldesign/fractalsvelte-ui/motion` — spring physics, the JS spring engine,
motion attachments, spring transitions and view transitions.
